title: Model fit heuristics + benchmark signals — Aurora Systems
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-14 16:00 PDT
Duration: 49 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-20260514-aurora-98432
Shared artifacts: demo deck (https://redwood.example/demo-deck), bench-spreadsheet.csv (link shared in chat), console screenshot link (redwood.console/snap/1243)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We want to walk through the model catalog heuristics, bench signals, and routing + compatibility matrix inside the Console and how that plugs into Optimize. Julian will drive the demo and I'll cover the commercial bits at the end.

[00:18] Nina Soto: Hi, good afternoon. Quick note — we're primarily evaluating for a search-relevance and summarization flow, some multi-turn chat in product support. Our timeline is Q3 pilot and possible Dedicated in Q4. Key constraints are 90ms P95 for short completions, and SOC2 + SSO support.

[00:35] Julian Kim: Great, that's helpful. Quick qual: what's your current stack — are you using managed endpoints or self-hosted?

[00:42] Derek Voss: We're on AWS today, using a mixture — some in-house GPU pool (k8s) for heavy batch jobs, but most calling OpenAI via API for prod. Looking to cut cost per token and improve tail latency.

[00:55] Samir Rao: We also have an internal constraint: all customer PII must not leave our VPC for now. So the Private deployment option is interesting, but we need to understand the tradeoffs.

[01:06] Julian Kim: Understood. We'll show hosted first, then how we'd map that to Dedicated/Private with VPC peering and KMS integrations.

[01:15] Maya Patel: Quick agenda: 1) model catalog walkthrough (focus on open models), 2) bench signal interpretation (latency/cost/quality), 3) compatibility matrices & kernel mapping, 4) routing policies and canary.

[01:28] -- screen share starts --

[02:00] Julian Kim: Opening Console — Catalog tab. Here you can filter by architecture, sequence length, quantization available, and performance profile. I'll type "open" to show open-source models only.

[02:20] Julian Kim: Notice the bench tiles on the right — they show throughput and P95 latency on the redwood-hosted profile. Important caveat: bench numbers are workload-specific. We attach a bench set id to each run (see bench-spreadsheet.csv).

[03:05] Nina Soto: How often do you refresh these bench runs? Sometimes model performance moves fast with new kernels.

[03:12] Julian Kim: Yeah, we re-run major runs weekly and tag model versions. For kernel-level updates (like new attention kernels), we run a focused regression pipeline and surface diffs. The Console shows "bench freshness" with dates.

[03:40] Julian Kim: Now opening the compatibility matrix view — rows are models, columns are runtime/hardware combos. Cells show green/yellow/red and a short note (eg: "good fit, 16GB GPU, int8 quant ok"). Click a cell to get kernel mapping and recommended quantization profile.

[04:05] Derek Voss: That kernel mapping — we run our own on-prem nodes. Can you export the kernel flags or is it only advisory?

[04:13] Julian Kim: You can export a YAML profile with quantization, kernel selection, and recommended batch sizes. For Private we can also provide a pre-built runtime container with those settings.

[04:35] -- 05:00 cut: small audio dropout --

[04:55] Julian Kim: Now show the bench signal page. Each model has multiple signals: latency P50/P95, token cost, token quality (BLEU/ROUGE for bench set, and a more opaque "alignment score" for chat flows). We color code regressions and let you pin a model to a route.

[05:20] Nina Soto: This "alignment score" — can you explain how it's computed? We need to map it to our internal evals.

[05:28] Sofia Alvarez: It's a composite: majority vote across prompt families + lexical similarity + some human-annotated calibration. It's meant to be a signal, not a definitive metric. We recommend running your test prompts (the Console supports uploading eval prompt sets) and then we compute delta vs our baseline.

[05:55] Samir Rao: Cool, can we bring our prompts? We want to see how the open models do on our short support snippets.

[06:04] Julian Kim: Absolutely — upload prompts in the Evals tab. We can also schedule a bench sprint where Redwood runs the suite and returns a CSV with token breakdowns.

[06:18] Maya Patel: For the pilot, we'd usually run a 2-week bench sprint: initial catalog shortlist -> Redwood runs bench on hosted + a dedicated small pool -> we look at regressions and then scope Private packaging if needed.

[06:35] Derek Voss: Pricing question — how do you bill bench runs and the hosted trial?

[06:42] Maya Patel: Bench runs are usually free for pilots but big custom runs may have a small service fee. Hosted API usage billed per token; Dedicated is reserved pricing. I can share a pilot pricing note after this call.

[07:00] Julian Kim: Back to technicals — here's the routing policy editor. You can define policies by latency SLO, cost cap, region, or a custom predicate (header, user tier). We support fallbacks to smaller quantized variants if the primary can't meet SLO.

[07:25] Nina Soto: Example: if user is premium, route to a higher-cost low-latency model; else route to quantized cheaper model?

[07:31] Julian Kim: Exactly. We'll demo a simple rule: if header x-user-tier==premium -> model A, else model B-quant8. Also show autoscaling and burst capacity.

[08:05] Julian Kim: Now a quick look at Optimize — this is the cost/perf suggestions engine. It ingests your traffic profile and recommends batch sizes, caching prefixes, and whether model quantization will keep quality within a delta.

[08:30] Samir Rao: How deterministic are these suggestions? We're worried about a model having a hidden quality drop after quantization.

[08:38] Sofia Alvarez: We return a confidence band and example prompt diffs. For high-risk flows we tag the change as "requires human review" and you can schedule a regression alert.

[09:05] -- timestamp jump to bench CSV demo --

[09:20] Julian Kim: Opening bench-spreadsheet.csv. Column examples: bench_id, model_name, hw_target, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, bleu, rouge, alignment_delta. See this row: vicuna-13b-v1 | a100-80g | p95 110ms | cost $0.021/token | alignment_delta +0.02 vs baseline.

[09:50] Derek Voss: That p95 looks a bit high for our 90ms SLO. Any levers?

[09:56] Julian Kim: Options: 1) use a lower-latency variant (llm-13b-optimized), 2) change to N-bit quantization combined with kernel mapping for lower memory copy overhead, 3) tune batching & enable prefix caching. The Console gives estimated impact of each change.

[10:25] Nina Soto: For Private, how does KMS integration work? We need envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys.

[10:33] Julian Kim: Private supports KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and partner HSM). The control plane can be run in customer VPC; you retain key custody. We'll surface audit logs and token-level tracing for full compliance.

[10:55] -- small crosstalk --

[11:10] Samir Rao: On the kernel mapping, you said there's an export. Will the exported runtime be just a set of flags or a precompiled binary?

[11:19] Julian Kim: For common open models we can provide a precompiled runtime image tuned to your hardware, or just the flags if you want to compile yourself. We also publish our kernel compatibility matrix for community review.

[11:40] Derek Voss: Any competitors you see customers move to for similar use cases?

[11:44] Maya Patel: Some customers evaluate Scale, Cohere, and major cloud provider endpoints like AWS Bedrock for simple use cases. The differentiator for us is the unified view across hosted/dedicated/private and the Optimize toolkit for cost control.

[12:05] -- 12:30 brief pause while Maya pulls a doc --

[12:40] Julian Kim: Now a short demo of an A/B canary. We create two routes: route A -> model optimized-int8; route B -> baseline float16. We'll send a small traffic golden set and compare quality & latency side-by-side in the Console.

[13:05] Nina Soto: If the canary fails on a specific prompt family, can we rollback automatically?

[13:12] Julian Kim: Yes — rollback policies can be set to auto-fallback on quality delta or latency breach. We can also set alerting to Slack or webhook.

[13:30] Samir Rao: We have an SSO requirement — SAML 2.0 with SCIM.

[13:36] Sofia Alvarez: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; can show the admin setup flow. For Private we can integrate your IdP directly.

[13:50] Derek Voss: Any documented SOC/ISO compliance artifacts?

[13:55] Maya Patel: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 material we can share under NDA. I'll add that to action items.

[14:12] -- 14:25 audio artifact: client asks about data residency --

[14:30] Nina Soto: Data residency — some EU customers require EU-only processing. Can Redwood pin a model to region?

[14:36] Julian Kim: Absolutely. Routing can include region constraints and the platform supports region-scoped model catalogs and footprints. For Private, obviously you control the location.

[15:00] -- deeper bench discussion --

[15:10] Julian Kim: One nuance on cost: our token cost numbers include GPU amortized + runtime overhead. For Dedicated we break down the unit economics so you can see what portion is ops + infra.

[15:30] Nina Soto: We want an apples-to-apples with our current OpenAI spend. Can Redwood normalize cost per 1k tokens and show expected monthly spend for our traffic profile?

[15:40] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, Optimize can take your traffic (we accept a sample CSV) and produce a monthly spend projection across routing policies. That output is what we use to size Dedicated pools.

[16:05] -- 16:20 small transcription glitch: "KV cash" instead of KV cache --

[16:25] Derek Voss: One more on quantization: do you have examples where quant8 caused hallucination regression? We've seen that with some models.

[16:33] Julian Kim: It happens. That's why Optimize flags risky families. For the support domain, we usually see minimal delta for short prompts but caution on long generative flows. We suggest a staged rollout with canary and automated prompt-level checks.

[17:00] -- 17:10 Julian shares export YAML --

[17:20] Julian Kim: Exported profile example: model: vicuna-13b-v2; quant: int8; kernel_flags: [fused_attn_v2, memcpy_opt]; batch_size: 8; prefetch_kv: true. (Note: some runtime strings may be abbreviated in the UI).

[17:55] Nina Soto: What's the typical uplift in latency when enabling prefix caching?

[18:02] Julian Kim: For session-based chat with reuse, prefix/KV caching can reduce p95 by 30-60% depending on reuse ratio. For single-shot short prompts it's minimal.

[18:25] Samir Rao: If we run the pilot on hosted but need Private later, what's the migration path for evaluations and bench results?

[18:33] Sofia Alvarez: Bench results are portable — they tie to model/version and bench-set id. When you move to Private we replicate the chosen runtime settings and re-run a short verification to confirm parity.

[18:55] Maya Patel: Quick recap: we'll run a bench sprint focused on your support prompts and short summarization flows. We'll provide a shortlist of models with kernel mappings and an expected cost/latency projection.

[19:10] Nina Soto: Sounds good. A few stakeholders who need to see the output: Priya (CTO), our legal (for SOC2), and platform infra (Derek).

[19:20] Derek Voss: Also, we want a simple export of the YAML runtime so our infra team can test on our k8s nodes.

[19:30] Maya Patel: Action items and next steps — I'll send the pilot scoping doc and pilot pricing. Julian, can you do the bench-run request?

[19:36] Julian Kim: Yep, I'll initiate a bench sprint once I have the prompt set and a sample traffic CSV. I'll put the initial bench run into the sheet and tag it with bench_id.

[19:50] -- 20:00 short QA --

[20:30] Priya Menon: Anything we should watch out for in terms of vendor lock? We like open tooling.

[20:38] Maya Patel: We try to avoid lock-in: exports, YAMLs, and runtime flags are portable; models are open. For Private you can host everything yourself.

[21:05] -- final minutes: pricing and security wrap --

[21:20] Maya Patel: I'll share: 1) pilot pricing note, 2) SOC2/ISO artifacts (NDA link), 3) bench-spreadsheet with sample runs, 4) console snapshot + instructions to upload eval prompts. Expect an email by Monday.

[21:40] Nina Soto: Great, thanks. Any left questions?

[21:45] Derek Voss: None from infra. We'll send the prompt set by EOD Friday.

[21:52] Maya Patel: Perfect. Appreciate your time. We'll follow up with the next meeting invite for bench sprint kickoff.

[22:00] -- call ends --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" -> KV cache), speakers labels were manual in parts. Transcript transcribed automatically and lightly edited for readability.
summary: Redwood demo of Console catalog, bench signals, compatibility matrix, kernel mapping, and Optimize recommendations. Customer (Aurora Systems) is evaluating open models for support and summarization flows with tight latency SLOs and SOC2 requirements. Agreement to run a bench sprint on uploaded prompt set and provide exportable runtime YAML and security artifacts.

Julian: Start bench sprint after prompt set and sample traffic CSV received (init bench_id in spreadsheet)

Aurora (Samir/Derek): Upload prompt set and sample traffic CSV (by 2026-05-15)

Redwood to run 2-week bench sprint and return bench-spreadsheet.csv
